answer: The most convincing defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers: every transaction countersigned by a sample of identity-staked verifiers, and anyone who countersigns an invalid one forfeits their stake automatically, with the loss set far above the delta between honest and dishonest epoch rewards, so betrayal is always net-negative. The pearl of the design is that identity itself becomes capital: creating fake sybil identities is cheap, but arming each with enough slashable stake to verify is expensive, and mass corruption risks total forfeiture.
